records.quote: Let X1 ~ MOEGE(alpha_1, eta, rho) and X2 ~ MOEGE(alpha_2, eta, rho). The random variable X1 is stochastically smaller than X2 in the: Stochastic order (X1 <=st X2) if F_X1(x) >= F_X2(x) for all x; Hazard rate order (X1 <=hr X2) if h_X1(x) >= h_X2(x) for all x; Likelihood ratio order (X1 <=lr X2) if f_X1(x)/f_X2(x) is a decreasing function. ... d/dx log(f1/f2) = 2 rho eta e^{-rho x}(1-e^{-rho x})^{eta-1}[alpha_1/(1 - alpha_1-bar(1-(1-e^{-rho x})^eta)) - alpha_2/(1 - alpha_2-bar(1-(1-e^{-rho x})^eta))] < 0 if alpha_1 < alpha_2 for all x > 0. Then it follows from the implications of stochastic ordering that: X1 <=lr X2 => X1 <=hr X2 => X1 <=st X2.
